question: The Guide is a 1958 novel written in English by the Indian author ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is RK Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Guide" (1958) is a celebrated English novel written by the Indian author R. K. Narayan (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami). (आर. के. नारायण)

• The novel is set in Narayan's fictional town of Malgudi and tells the story of Raju, a tourist guide who is transformed into a spiritual guide and finally into a reluctant holy man.

• It won him the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1960 and was made into the Hindi film "Guide" (1965) starring Dev Anand and Waheeda Rehman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous works of R. K. Narayan: Swami and Friends (1935), The Bachelor of Arts, The Dark Room, The English Teacher, The Financial Expert, The Man-Eater of Malgudi, The Vendor of Sweets, Malgudi Days (short stories).

• Option 1 Mulk Raj Anand wrote Untouchable, Coolie, Two Leaves and a Bud.

• Option 2 Khushwant Singh wrote Train to Pakistan, I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale, Delhi: A Novel.

• Option 4 Nirad C. Chaudhuri wrote The Autobiography of an Unknown Indian.

NOTE

• R. K. Narayan was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1964) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000), and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 1989.

• Along with Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao, he is regarded as one of the "Big Three" of early Indian English fiction.

question: The stretch between Mumbai to Goa of western coast of India is known as _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Konkan coast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The western coastal plain of India is divided into segments, and the stretch from Daman/Mumbai in the north to Goa in the south is called the Konkan Coast. (कोंकण तट)

• It is a narrow plain lying between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats (Sahyadri), noted for its ports, backwaters, estuaries and the famous Alphonso mango and cashew cultivation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Divisions of the Western Coastal Plain (north to south): Kachchh & Kathiawar coast (Gujarat) → Konkan Coast (Mumbai to Goa) → Kanara/Karnataka Coast (Goa to Mangaluru) → Malabar Coast (Mangaluru to Kanniyakumari, Kerala).

• Option 1 Coromandel Coast lies on the eastern side of India (Tamil Nadu–Andhra Pradesh), not the west.

• Option 3 Malabar Coast is the southern-most stretch of the western coast, famous for its lagoons and backwaters (kayals).

NOTE

• The Eastern Coastal Plain is divided into the Northern Circars (Odisha–Andhra) and the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu).

• The Konkan Railway, one of India's engineering marvels, runs along this coast connecting Roha (Maharashtra) to Thokur (Karnataka).

question: Which of the following autobiographies is NOT correctly matched with the concerned cricketer?
option_1: Playing it My Way – VVS Laxman
option_2: The Test of My Life: From Cricket to Cancer and Back – Yuvraj Singh
option_3: Straight from the Heart – Kapil Dev
solution_text:
The correct answer is Playing it My Way – VVS Laxman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Playing It My Way" (2014) is the autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar, not of VVS Laxman. Hence this pair is NOT correctly matched. (सचिन तेंदुलकर)

• VVS Laxman's autobiography is titled "281 and Beyond" (2018), named after his historic 281 against Australia at Eden Gardens in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is correct: "The Test of My Life: From Cricket to Cancer and Back" — Yuvraj Singh (2013).

• Option 3 is correct: "Straight from the Heart" — Kapil Dev (2004).

• Option 4 is correct: "Cricket Delightful" — Syed Mushtaq Ali (1967).

NOTE

• Other cricket books frequently asked in SSC: A Century Is Not Enough (Sourav Ganguly), The Race of My Life (Milkha Singh, athletics), Sunny Days and Idols (Sunil Gavaskar), Anything but Chutney (Aakash Chopra), No Spin (Shane Warne), Believe: What Life and Cricket Taught Me (Suresh Raina).

• Sachin Tendulkar is the only cricketer to receive the Bharat Ratna (2014).

question: What does El Niño refer to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hot water current.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• El Niño is a warm (hot) ocean current that appears off the coast of Peru and Ecuador in the eastern Pacific Ocean, usually around Christmas time. (उष्ण जलधारा)

• The name "El Niño" is Spanish for "the little boy / the Christ Child", because fishermen noticed the warming around December.

• It replaces the cold Peru (Humboldt) Current, raising sea-surface temperatures, reducing the upwelling of nutrients and thereby harming the fishing industry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• El Niño is the oceanic component of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO); the atmospheric component is the Southern Oscillation (a see-saw of air pressure between Tahiti and Darwin).

• In India, El Niño years are usually associated with a weak South-West monsoon and drought conditions.

• La Niña is the opposite phase — abnormally cold water in the eastern Pacific, generally linked to a good Indian monsoon.

NOTE

• Warm currents: Gulf Stream, Kuroshio, North Atlantic Drift, Brazil Current, Agulhas Current.

• Cold currents: Labrador, Peru (Humboldt), Benguela, Canary, California, Oyashio Current.

question: Where was the 13th Hockey India senior women’s national hockey championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 13th Hockey India Senior Women's National Championship 2023 was held at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh. (आंध्र प्रदेश)

• Hockey Jharkhand and Hockey Haryana were among the leading teams in the tournament, which is the premier domestic women's hockey competition organised by Hockey India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Hockey India is the national governing body for the sport in India, recognised by the International Hockey Federation (FIH) and the Indian Olympic Association.

• The Indian women's hockey team finished a historic fourth at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held 2021), and won the bronze medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, Birmingham.

• Rani Rampal captained the team to that Olympic performance; she received the Khel Ratna and Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Hockey is played 11-a-side on a turf field; the FIH was founded in 1924 and has its headquarters at Lausanne, Switzerland.

• India's men's hockey team has won 8 Olympic gold medals, the last in Moscow 1980, and bronze medals at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advice the President in the exercise of the President's functions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 74.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 74 of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. (अनुच्छेद 74)

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 made the advice binding on the President; the 44th Amendment, 1978 allowed the President to return the advice once for reconsideration, after which he must act upon it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 75 — provisions relating to the appointment, tenure, responsibility, oath and salaries of Ministers; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

• Option 1 Article 77 — deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India (all executive action is expressed in the name of the President).

• Option 3 Article 71 — matters relating to the election of the President and Vice-President and disputes about it.

• Option 4 Article 72 — the pardoning power of the President (pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, commutation).

NOTE

• Corresponding State-level Articles: Article 163 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor) and Article 164 (appointment of the Chief Minister and other Ministers).

• The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 limits the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the strength of the Lok Sabha/State Legislative Assembly.

question: Which of the following is a key objective of Micro Finance Institutions in India?
option_1: Providing loans exclusively to women entrepreneurs
option_4: Promoting financial inclusion and poverty alleviation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promoting financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) provide small-value loans and other basic financial services to low-income households, small entrepreneurs and self-help groups who have little or no access to formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाएँ)

• Their key objective is therefore financial inclusion and poverty alleviation — bringing the unbanked into the formal financial system and helping them build livelihoods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because although a very large share of microfinance borrowers are women, MFIs do not lend exclusively to women entrepreneurs.

• Option 2 is wrong — MFIs finance micro and small activities, not large-scale industry, which is served by banks and development financial institutions.

• Option 3 is wrong — profit maximisation for shareholders is the objective of ordinary commercial firms, not the defining objective of microfinance.

NOTE

• In India, NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India; the Malegam Committee (2011) framed the regulatory approach after the 2010 Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis.

• SIDBI and NABARD are key refinancing institutions; the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme launched by NABARD in 1992 is the world's largest microfinance programme.

• Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh, founder of the Grameen Bank, is called the "father of microfinance" and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

question: _____________ is one of the most important festivals of Kamakhya temple of Guwahati. It is held every year during the monsoon (mid-June) season, when the temple is closed for three days for tantric rites.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ambubachi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ambubachi Mela is the most important annual festival of the Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati (Assam). (अम्बुबाची मेला)

• It is held during the monsoon (mid-June, Assamese month of Ahaar) and symbolises the annual menstruation of the goddess Kamakhya / Mother Earth. The temple remains closed for three days, and is reopened on the fourth day after purification and tantric rites.

• It is often called the "Mahakumbh of the East" because of the huge gathering of tantriks, sadhus and pilgrims.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Bihu — the chief festival of Assam, celebrated in three forms: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April, spring/new year), Kati/Kongali Bihu (October) and Magh/Bhogali Bihu (January, harvest).

• Option 3 Baishagu — the spring festival of the Bodo tribe of Assam, celebrated in mid-April.

• Option 4 Me-Dum-Me-Phi — festival of the Ahom community of Assam (31 January), celebrated in memory of ancestors.

NOTE

• The Kamakhya Temple on the Nilachal Hill is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, associated with the fall of the yoni (womb) of Sati.

• Other important Assam facts: capital Dispur, Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhinoceros), Majuli (world's largest river island), Brahmaputra river.

question: In which city is the Kamakhya temple situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guwahati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kamakhya Temple is situated on the Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, on the southern bank of the Brahmaputra river. (गुवाहाटी, असम)

• It is dedicated to the goddess Kamakhya, a form of Shakti, and is one of the oldest and most revered of the 51 Shakti Peethas.

• The present structure was rebuilt in the 16th century by King Nara Narayan of the Koch dynasty, in the distinctive Nilachal style (hemispherical dome over a cruciform base).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Dehradun — capital of Uttarakhand; nearby are Tapkeshwar Temple and the Forest Research Institute.

• Option 2 Bhopal — capital of Madhya Pradesh; near the UNESCO site Sanchi Stupa and Bhimbetka rock shelters.

• Option 4 Indore — the commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh; famous for Rajwada and Lal Bagh Palace.

NOTE

• Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and of the North-East; it is called the "Gateway of North-East India".

• Other Shakti Peethas frequently asked: Vaishno Devi (J&K), Kalighat (Kolkata), Jwalamukhi (Himachal Pradesh), Naina Devi (Himachal Pradesh), Ambaji (Gujarat).

question: Which of the following statements best defines a Micro Finance Institution (MFI)?
option_1: MFIs are investment firms that cater exclusively to high-net-worth individuals.
option_2: MFIs are non-profit organisations that provide financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses.
option_3: MFIs are banks that provide loans only to large corporations.
option_4: MFIs are government agencies that regulate the microfinance sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is MFIs are non-profit organisations that provide financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Micro Finance Institution (MFI) is an organisation that offers small loans (microcredit), savings, insurance and remittance facilities to low-income individuals, self-help groups and small businesses that are excluded from mainstream banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्था)

• Traditionally MFIs began as not-for-profit societies, trusts and NGOs whose purpose was social development rather than profit, which is exactly what Option 2 states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — catering to high-net-worth individuals is the work of wealth-management and private-banking firms, the very opposite of microfinance.

• Option 3 is wrong — lending only to large corporations describes corporate/wholesale banking, not microfinance.

• Option 4 is wrong — the regulator of the microfinance sector in India is the Reserve Bank of India, not the MFIs themselves.

NOTE

• Legal forms of MFIs in India: NGO-MFIs (societies/trusts), Section 8 companies, cooperatives and NBFC-MFIs (the most common commercial form, regulated by the RBI).

• Key features of microcredit: small ticket size, collateral-free lending, group guarantee (joint liability), frequent repayment, and a focus on women borrowers.

• Well-known Indian MFIs: Bandhan (later a universal bank), Bharat Financial Inclusion (SKS), Ujjivan, Equitas, CreditAccess Grameen.

question: Mumbai Indians defeated which team to win Women’s Premier League in March, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi Capitals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the final of the inaugural Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023, played on 26 March 2023 at the Brabourne Stadium, Mumbai, the Mumbai Indians defeated the Delhi Capitals by 7 wickets to lift the title. (दिल्ली कैपिटल्स)

• Harmanpreet Kaur captained the champion Mumbai Indians; Meg Lanning captained Delhi Capitals.

• Nat Sciver-Brunt scored an unbeaten 60 in the final and was adjudged Player of the Match.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The five teams of the first WPL season were Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Royal Challengers Bangalore, UP Warriorz and Gujarat Giants.

• Hayley Matthews (Mumbai Indians) was the Player of the Tournament; the Orange Cap went to Meg Lanning and the Purple Cap to Hayley Matthews.

• In WPL 2024, Royal Challengers Bangalore beat Delhi Capitals to win the title, and in WPL 2025 Mumbai Indians won again.

NOTE

• The WPL is organised by the BCCI; its first season was played in Mumbai (DY Patil Stadium and Brabourne Stadium).

• India's women's team achievements: runners-up in the ICC Women's World Cup 2005 and 2017, gold at the 2022 Commonwealth Games (silver), and champions of the 2022 Asia Cup.

question: The Songi Mukhawate dance of ___________ celebrates the victory of truth over falsehood. The name of the dance is derived from the two lion masks worn by two dancers who represent Narasimha, an aspect of Lord Vishnu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Songi Mukhawate is a traditional masked folk dance of Maharashtra. (महाराष्ट्र)

• Two dancers wear lion masks representing Narasimha, the man-lion incarnation (avatar) of Lord Vishnu, and the performance symbolises the victory of truth (satya) over falsehood (asatya) — recalling Narasimha's slaying of the demon Hiranyakashipu.

• "Songi" refers to masked impersonation and "Mukhawate" refers to the masks worn by the performers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Maharashtra: Lavani, Tamasha, Povada (Powada), Dhangari Gaja, Koli, Dindi, Kala, Lezim.

• Option 1 Madhya Pradesh — Matki, Gaur, Grida, Maanch, Karma, Phulpati.

• Option 2 Jharkhand — Chhau (Seraikella), Paika, Jhumar, Karma, Domkach.

• Option 4 Gujarat — Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Bhavai, Padhar.

NOTE

• Other masked dance traditions of India: Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/West Bengal — inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2010), Cham (Ladakh/Sikkim Buddhist monastic dance), Theyyam (Kerala), Gambhira (West Bengal).

• Narasimha Jayanti is celebrated on the Chaturdashi of the bright fortnight of Vaishakha.

question: Who among the following is best known for creating a fusion style of dance by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uday Shankar (1900–1977) is celebrated for creating a fusion or "Uday Shankar style" of dance, blending European theatrical stagecraft and ballet techniques with Indian classical and folk dance. (उदय शंकर)

• He worked with the legendary Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova in the 1920s, choreographing pieces such as "Radha–Krishna", and later took Indian dance to audiences across Europe and America.

• He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora (1938) and produced the pioneering dance film "Kalpana" (1948).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Yamini Krishnamurthy — a renowned exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi; Padma Vibhushan (2016).

• Option 3 Gopi Krishna — a famous Kathak dancer, remembered for the film Jhanak Jhanak Payal Baaje.

• Option 4 Sonal Mansingh — an eminent Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer; Padma Vibhushan and later a Rajya Sabha member.

NOTE

• Uday Shankar was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1971) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (1962).

• He was the elder brother of the sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar, and his son Ananda Shankar was a noted musician.

question: Where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association founded in 1928?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in September 1928 at a meeting held in the ruins of the Feroz Shah Kotla fort in Delhi. (दिल्ली — फिरोज शाह कोटला)

• It was a reorganisation of the earlier Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), founded in 1924 at Kanpur by Ram Prasad Bismil, Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee. The word "Socialist" was added on the initiative of Bhagat Singh.

• Key members: Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sukhdev, Shivaram Rajguru, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Jatindra Nath Das.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Major actions associated with the HSRA: the Saunders murder (Lahore, December 1928) avenging Lala Lajpat Rai's death, and the Central Legislative Assembly bomb-and-leaflet action (8 April 1929) by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, with the slogan "Inquilab Zindabad".

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged at Lahore on 23 March 1931, observed as Shaheed Diwas.

• Chandrashekhar Azad died at Alfred Park, Allahabad on 27 February 1931.

NOTE

• Related events: Kakori Conspiracy (9 August 1925) by the HRA — Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in 1927.

• Bhagat Singh's writings include the famous essay "Why I am an Atheist" (1930).

question: Which process is sometimes called "reduction division" because it reduces the number of chromosomes to half the normal number to form sperm and eggs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meiosis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meiosis is called "reduction division" because it halves the chromosome number — a diploid (2n) germ cell produces four haploid (n) daughter cells, i.e. the gametes (sperm and eggs). (अर्धसूत्री विभाजन)

• In humans, a cell with 46 chromosomes (2n) produces gametes with 23 chromosomes (n), so that fertilisation restores the diploid number.

• Meiosis occurs in two successive stages — Meiosis I (reductional) and Meiosis II (equational) — with only one round of DNA replication.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Amitosis — a simple direct division of the nucleus without spindle formation or chromosome condensation, seen in bacteria and some degenerating cells.

• Option 3 Cytokinesis — the division of the cytoplasm that follows nuclear division.

• Option 4 Karyokinesis — the division of the nucleus itself (the term applies to both mitosis and meiosis).

NOTE

• Mitosis is the equational division — one parent cell produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells; it is responsible for growth and repair.

• Stages of both divisions: Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase. Crossing over (recombination) occurs during the pachytene stage of Prophase I of meiosis, which is the main source of genetic variation.

question: Which chemical element with atomic number 35 has a dark reddish-brown liquid with a burning pungent odour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bromine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bromine (Br) has the atomic number 35 and is a dark reddish-brown liquid with a sharp, pungent, suffocating smell. (ब्रोमीन)

• It is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature (mercury is the only liquid metal), and it belongs to Group 17 — the halogens.

• The name comes from the Greek "bromos" meaning stench, because of its irritating odour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Tennessine (Ts) — a synthetic, radioactive superheavy halogen with atomic number 117.

• Option 2 Chlorine (Cl) — atomic number 17, a greenish-yellow gas with a pungent smell, used for water disinfection.

• Option 3 Astatine (At) — atomic number 85, an extremely rare radioactive halogen.

NOTE

• The halogens (Group 17): Fluorine (9), Chlorine (17), Bromine (35), Iodine (53), Astatine (85), Tennessine (117). Their physical states at room temperature: F and Cl are gases, Br is a liquid, I and At are solids.

• Uses of bromine: silver bromide in photographic films, flame retardants, and potassium bromide in medicine.

• Iodine deficiency causes goitre; fluorine excess causes fluorosis.

question: In which year did Pakistan win the Kabaddi (Circle style) World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pakistan won the Kabaddi World Cup (Circle Style) in 2020, defeating India in the final held at Punjab Stadium, Lahore (Pakistan) in February 2020. (पाकिस्तान — 2020)

• This was Pakistan's first Circle-style Kabaddi World Cup title; India had won every previous edition of the tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Circle Style Kabaddi World Cup was first organised in 2010 at Punjab, India, and India won the editions of 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2016.

• Circle style (Punjabi) kabaddi is played on a circular field and differs from the standard/national style played on a rectangular court, which is the format used in the Asian Games and the Pro Kabaddi League.

• The Standard Style Kabaddi World Cup (2004, 2007, 2016) has been won by India on every occasion.

NOTE

• Kabaddi has been part of the Asian Games since 1990 (Beijing); India has dominated both the men's and women's events.

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was launched in 2014; the sport's governing bodies are the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI) and the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF).

question: The North–South corridor, which is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, links which two cities of India from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Srinagar and Kanyakumari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The North–South Corridor links Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) in the north with Kanniyakumari (Tamil Nadu) in the south, with a spur to Kochi. Its length is about 4,076 km. (श्रीनगर – कन्याकुमारी)

• It is part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), undertaken along with the Golden Quadrilateral.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The East–West Corridor links Silchar (Assam) in the east with Porbandar (Gujarat) in the west, about 3,640 km long.

• The Golden Quadrilateral (about 5,846 km) connects the four metropolitan cities — Delhi – Kolkata – Chennai – Mumbai – Delhi. It was launched in 1998–2001 under the NHDP.

• Both corridors intersect at Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh).

NOTE

• National Highways constitute about 2% of India's road length but carry about 40% of road traffic.

• NH-44 (earlier NH-7) is the longest national highway in India, running from Srinagar to Kanniyakumari.

• The NHAI was constituted by an Act of Parliament in 1988 and became operational in 1995.

question: For which community was a journal Rast Goftar started for the purpose of social-religious reforms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parsis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rast Goftar" (meaning "Truth Teller") was a Gujarati-language weekly started in 1851 by Dadabhai Naoroji (along with Kharshedji Nusserwanji Cama) for the social and religious reform of the Parsi community. (पारसी समुदाय)

• It was the mouthpiece of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (Religious Reform Association), founded in 1851 in Bombay by Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, S. S. Bengalee and K. N. Cama.

• The reformers campaigned against orthodox rituals and for women's education, the abolition of child marriage and reform of Parsi law relating to marriage and inheritance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji is called the "Grand Old Man of India"; he authored "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", propounding the Drain of Wealth theory, and was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892).

• Other reform journals: Sambad Kaumudi (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Bengali), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Ram Mohan Roy, Persian), Kesari and Maratha (Bal Gangadhar Tilak), Al-Hilal (Maulana Abul Kalam Azad), Indian Mirror, Amrita Bazar Patrika.

NOTE

• Other social-reform movements: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang), Arya Samaj (1875, Dayanand Saraswati), Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan), Singh Sabha Movement (1873, Sikhs).

question: 26 January was selected as the date of the inauguration of the Constitution because on the same date in 1930, the Indian National Congress had revealed ________________________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purna Swaraj Movement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950, a date deliberately chosen because on 26 January 1930 the Indian National Congress had publicly proclaimed Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) and celebrated it as the first Independence Day. (पूर्ण स्वराज)

• The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at the Lahore Session of the Congress in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, where the tricolour was unfurled on the banks of the Ravi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Quit India Movement — launched on 8 August 1942 from Bombay (Gowalia Tank) with Gandhi's slogan "Do or Die".

• Option 3 Namak Satyagraha (Dandi March) — began 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi on 6 April 1930, marking the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

• Option 4 Khilafat Movement — 1919–1924, led by the Ali brothers (Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali), supported by Gandhi and linked with the Non-Cooperation Movement.

NOTE

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas), and it came into effect on 26 January 1950.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.

question: What is the name of the scheme launched by Uttar Pradesh government to boost milk production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nand Baba Milk Mission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nand Baba Milk Mission (Nand Baba Dugdh Mission) was launched by the Government of Uttar Pradesh to boost milk production, strengthen dairy cooperatives and improve the income of milk producers. (नंद बाबा दुग्ध मिशन)

• The mission provides for setting up milk producer committees in villages, subsidies for dairy units and improved cattle breeds, and better milk collection and marketing infrastructure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh is the largest milk-producing state in India, followed by Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

• Central schemes for dairying: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (indigenous bovine breed development, launched 2014), National Programme for Dairy Development, Dairy Entrepreneurship Development Scheme, and the National Animal Disease Control Programme.

• Operation Flood (launched 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board under Dr. Verghese Kurien) made India the world's largest milk producer — the "White Revolution".

NOTE

• Dr. Verghese Kurien is called the "Father of the White Revolution / Milkman of India"; the Amul cooperative model of Anand, Gujarat inspired the national programme.

• India accounts for roughly one-fourth of global milk production; National Milk Day is observed on 26 November (Kurien's birth anniversary).

question: What is the source of Directive Principles of State Policy?
option_1: The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1919
option_2: The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1935
option_3: The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1909
option_4: The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1947
solution_text:
The correct answer is The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1935.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution, were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland (1937), which had in turn taken the idea from the Spanish Constitution.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the DPSPs as "novel features" resembling the "Instrument of Instructions" issued to the Governor-General and Governors under the Government of India Act, 1935. (भारत शासन अधिनियम, 1935)

• Hence the source referred to in this question is the Instrument of Instructions of the GOI Act, 1935.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy, an All-India Federation (never implemented), a Federal Court (1937) and abolished dyarchy in the provinces while introducing it at the Centre.

• The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

• The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

NOTE

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (Article 37) but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

• Important DPSP Articles: 39 (equal pay, distribution of resources), 40 (village panchayats), 44 (Uniform Civil Code), 45 (early childhood care), 47 (nutrition and prohibition), 48A (environment), 50 (separation of judiciary from executive), 51 (international peace).

question: How many classical dance forms does the Sangeet Natak Akademi in India officially recognise, as of August 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognises eight (8) classical dance forms of India (as of August 2021). (आठ शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

• They are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh/North India), Kathakali (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Mohiniyattam (Kerala) and Sattriya (Assam).

• Sattriya, created by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardeva, was the last to be granted classical status, in 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Ministry of Culture lists nine forms by additionally including Chhau, which is why "9" is sometimes seen; but the Sangeet Natak Akademi figure asked here is 8.

• The Natya Shastra, written by Bharata Muni, is the foundational treatise of Indian classical dance and drama.

• Bharatanatyam is based on the Natya Shastra and was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam; Kathakali is a story-play form with elaborate make-up (Chutti).

NOTE

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, was set up in 1952/1953 with its headquarters at New Delhi; it confers the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and Fellowship (Ratna).

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati (Bharatanatyam); Birju Maharaj (Kathak); Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh (Odissi); Kanak Rele (Mohiniyattam).

question: According to the Human Development Report 2021-22, what is the rank of India among 191 countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 132.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Human Development Report 2021–22, released by the UNDP in September 2022, India ranked 132nd out of 191 countries and territories, with an HDI value of 0.633, placing it in the "medium human development" category. (भारत — 132वाँ स्थान)

• India had ranked 131 out of 189 in the previous report (2020), and the slight decline reflected the global fall in HDI during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Human Development Index (HDI) was devised in 1990 by Mahbub ul Haq (Pakistan) and Amartya Sen (India), and is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

• The HDI combines three dimensions: (i) a long and healthy life — life expectancy at birth; (ii) knowledge — mean and expected years of schooling; and (iii) a decent standard of living — GNI per capita (PPP).

• Switzerland topped the HDR 2021–22, followed by Norway and Iceland; South Sudan was last.

NOTE

• Other UNDP indices published with the HDR: Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII), Gender Development Index (GDI) and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

• The theme of the HDR 2021–22 was "Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives: Shaping our Future in a Transforming World".

question: Which Indian musical legend is credited with composing Talas such as Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M Balamuralikrishna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna (1930–2016) was a legendary Carnatic vocalist, composer and multi-instrumentalist credited with creating new talas such as Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi. (एम. बालमुरलीकृष्ण)

• He also devised new ragas including Mahati, Lavangi, Sidhdhi, Sumukham and Sarvashri, some using as few as three or four notes.

• He composed in several languages, sang more than 25,000 concerts worldwide, and was renowned for his Tyagaraja kritis and jugalbandis with Hindustani musicians such as Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and Hariprasad Chaurasia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Awards: Padma Shri (1971), Padma Bhushan (1991), Padma Vibhushan (2005), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, two National Film Awards for Best Male Playback Singer, and France's Chevalier of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres.

• Option 2 Bade Ghulam Ali Khan — Hindustani vocalist of the Patiala gharana ("Ke Karan Aayo Balam", "Yaad Piya Ki Aaye").

• Option 3 K. J. Yesudas — celebrated playback singer and Carnatic vocalist from Kerala.

• Option 4 Pandit Jasraj — doyen of the Mewati gharana of Hindustani classical music.

NOTE

• Carnatic music's "Trinity" comprises Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

• Basic concepts: raga (melodic framework), tala (rhythmic cycle), sruti (pitch) and swara (note). Purandara Dasa is called the "Father of Carnatic Music".
